## Findings
- claim-1: Under the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation and \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\), let \(p=c=1\), \(a=1\), \(b=3\). Then \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), \(\min(i,j)=3\), and \(d=ij\). Put \[ P_{x,y}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},y)}\quad(y=0\text{ omitted}). \] The complete Schur-column sets in degrees \(d+k\), \(0\le k\le3\), are \(\{P_{x,y}:x+y=k\}\).
- claim-2: Writing \[ X_k=P_{k,0},\quad Y_k=P_{0,k},\quad Z=P_{1,1},\quad A=P_{2,1},\quad B=P_{1,2}, \] the complete Pieri-row lattices are \[ \mathcal R_d=0,\qquad \mathcal R_{d+1}=\mathbb Z(X_1+Y_1), \] \[ \mathcal R_{d+2}= \mathbb Z(Z+Y_2)+\mathbb Z(X_2+Z), \] and \[ \mathcal R_{d+3}= \mathbb Z(X_3+A)+\mathbb Z(A+B)+\mathbb Z(B+Y_3). \]
- claim-3: Retaining the horizontal proposed family \[ F_X=(X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3), \] complementary minors in degrees \(d,d+1,d+2,d+3\) have determinants \(1,1,1,1\), respectively. In degrees \(d+2,d+3\), use rows \((X_2+Z,Z+Y_2)\) and \((X_3+A,A+B,B+Y_3)\), giving \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}_{(Z,Y_2)},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}_{(A,B,Y_3)}. \]
- claim-4: Retaining the vertical proposed family \[ F_Y=(X_0,Y_1,Y_2,Y_3), \] also gives complementary minors of determinant \(1\). In degrees \(d+2,d+3\), on complementary columns \((X_2,Z)\) and \((X_3,A,B)\), the same selected rows yield \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}. \]
- claim-5: Consequently, in the truncated quotient through degree \(d+3\), \[ \bar Y_1=-\bar X_1,\qquad \bar Y_2=\bar X_2,\qquad \bar Y_3=-\bar X_3, \] and each of \(F_X,F_Y\) is a degreewise integral basis of the truncated quotient.
- claim-6: The requested target—complete Pieri row lattices in degrees \(d,\ldots,d+3\) and explicit unimodular complementary minors retaining the four proposed generators—is established, conditional on the stated integral presentation hypotheses.
## Strategy
Under the stipulated integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, enumerate degree-\(d+k\) columns as \(P_{x,y}\) with \(x+y=k\), \(0\le k\le3\). Apply Pieri multiplication and use \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\) to identify the full product-row lattices. Select the displayed triangular complementary minors, retaining respectively \(F_X\) and \(F_Y\), each with determinant \(1\).

Thus the requested degree-\(\le d+3\) target is established conditionally on those presentation hypotheses.

## Gaps
This is a truncated calculation only. It does not establish an all-degree quotient description, ideal minimality, or any general \(a=1,b=3\) theorem beyond the specified doubly-boundary case \(p=c=1\).

## Next
Any extension requires separate enumeration and unimodular row-lattice certificates in degrees \(d+4\) and above, followed by an independent graded-globalization argument.
